title: On Hoping for a letter before Easter
subtitle: 价值观 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 价值观（做人与做事·价值观与人生意义）
meta: 主题语境：价值观（做人与做事·价值观与人生意义）　|　核心词汇：hope　|　正文 356 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 hope 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the driver ① hoped for a letter before Easter without a word of thanks, and every passenger in the station said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the driver ② hopes for a letter before Easter at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ hope for a letter before Easter at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ hoped for a letter before Easter before — a line in the timetable for February 1950 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Hoping for a letter before Easter without a word of thanks, the driver said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the ticket at the far platform, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ hope for better news in the morning at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Hope for better news in the morning at once and never mention it again.

By 1963 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the timetable, and a new passenger from the next station ⑧ hopes for better news in the morning without a word of thanks every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the platform, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ hoped for a letter before Easter again when nobody else would.

⑩ To hope for a letter before Easter, my mother said in 1968, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the station remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the station forgets, somebody hopes for a letter before Easter at once again and somebody must hope for a letter before Easter without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 希望（一般过去式 hoped for a letter before Easter：1956 年司机头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 希望（一般现在 hopes for a letter before Easter：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 希望（不定式 to hope for a letter before Easter：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 希望（过去完成时 had hoped for a letter before Easter：1950 年二月的时刻表上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 希望（动名词 hoping for a letter before Easter 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 盼望（hope for better news in the morning：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去盼望盼着早上有个更好的消息）
G. v. 盼望（hope for better news in the morning：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 希望（后段两处：新来的乘客照例 hopes for better news in the morning，而母亲又一次 hoped for a letter before Easter）

hope 意为“希望”，自那以后司机二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 hopes。
hope 意为“希望”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯希望指望复活节前能来一封信”，此处为不定式 to hope for a letter before Easter。
hope 意为“希望”，时刻表里 二月 那行字说明早在 1963 年之前就有人希望过，故用过去完成时 had hoped。
hope 意为“希望”，司机说“希望指望复活节前能来一封信这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 hoping for a letter before Easter 作主语。
hope 意为“盼望”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去盼望盼着早上有个更好的消息”，should ever 之后用原形 hope for better news in the morning。
hope 意为“盼望”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻盼望盼着早上有个更好的消息（hope for better news in the morning at once），以后再也不要提起。
hope 意为“希望”，新来的乘客每个日子都照例盼望盼着早上有个更好的消息，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 hopes。
hope 意为“希望”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢希望指望复活节前能来一封信，用一般过去式 hoped 叙述。
hope 意为“希望”，结尾那句是母亲 1968 年的话：要希望指望复活节前能来一封信，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和车站记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 hope 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1956 the driver hoped for a letter before Easter without a word of thanks, and nobody in the station forgot it.
Even now the driver hopes for a letter before Easter at once whenever the station asks.
Hoping for a letter before Easter without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever hope for better news in the morning at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new passenger from the next station hopes for better news in the morning without a word of thanks every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother hoped for a letter before Easter again, and the station remembered that half.
